transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, what brings me in is... it's about elevators. And small rooms, if the door gets locked. Whenever I step into a slow elevator or one of those tight spaces, my chest just jumps right away. I get this strong, immediate need to get back out before I can even think straight. It's just a sudden, overwhelming feeling every single time.
Do these sudden surges of anxiety ever happen completely out of the blue, when you are not in an elevator or small space?
No, not really. It's just when I'm in those spots. If I'm sitting at home or out for a walk, I'm fine. It only hits me when I'm actually in an elevator or a tiny room.
Do you feel this same kind of intense anxiety when you are in crowded places, such as a busy store or a concert?

No, crowds don't bother me much. I mean, I can go to the grocery store or be around a bunch of people just fine. It's really just the enclosed spaces, like I said, the elevators or small rooms. Being around a lot of people doesn't give me that same panicked feeling at all.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators and small spaces?

Well, it's been going on for about a year and a month now. It all started right after... well, I had a brief detention following a housing-rights demonstration. Ever since that happened, I've just had this trouble with elevators and tight spaces. So, yeah, a little over a year.
Do you experience recurrent unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks about that detention?

No, nothing like that. I don't have nightmares about it or, you know, flashbacks. I sleep just fine. I don't really sit around thinking about the detention itself... it's really just the actual physical feeling of being stuck in a small room now that gets to me. But no bad memories or anything keeping me up at night.
